paper.title_en: Static Magnetic Brane Solutions in Quartic Quasi-Topological Gravity with Power-Law Maxwell Nonlinear Electrodynamics
paper.abstract_en: In this paper, we investigate static magnetic brane solutions in (n+1)-dimensional quartic quasi-topological gravity coupled to power-law Maxwell nonlinear electrodynamics. We derive the corresponding solutions and analyze their geometric and physical properties. We observe that the solutions are horizonless and free of curvature singularities in the physically accessible region, while the spacetime generally exhibits a conical singularity with a nonzero angular deficit at the lower radial endpoint. We demonstrate that the endpoint is independent of the higher-curvature couplings lambda, mu, and c, whereas the near-endpoint geometry is mainly controlled by the magnetic parameter q and the nonlinear parameter s. At large radial distances, we find that the higher-curvature couplings govern the asymptotic behavior of the metric. We also establish that finite asymptotic solutions require 1/2 < s <= 2 and analyze the dependence of the angular deficit on q, s, and the endpoint parameter rho_+. Using the counterterm method, we calculate the conserved mass density and show that the static magnetic brane carries no net electric charge. Finally, we verify that the power-law Maxwell theory recovers linear Maxwell electrodynamics at s=1 and Einstein gravity when lambda=mu=c=0.
